"f42d077c-e368-53a5-991d-e999c0fb2c03" :question/problem "Find the general nonzero real solution to the differential equation

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}+2 \cdot \left(x+5\right) \cdot y=\left(x+5\right) \cdot y^{2}.
$$

Work on an interval where $\left(x+5\right)>0$. Choose constants and intervals on which the displayed expressions are real and finite.

{{selection}}"] [:db/add "f42d077c-e368-53a5-991d-e999c0fb2c03" :question/worked-solution "This is a Bernoulli equation with

$$\begin{aligned}p(x)&=2 \cdot \left(x+5\right)\\ q(x)&=\left(x+5\right)\\ n&=2.\end{aligned}$$

Divide by $y^{2}$ and set $z=y^{-1}$. The chain rule gives

$$\frac{\mathrm{d}z}{\mathrm{d}x}=- \frac{1}{y^{2}}\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}.$$

Hence the linear equation in standard form is

$$\frac{\mathrm{d}z}{\mathrm{d}x}+\left(- 2 \cdot \left(x+5\right)\right)z=- \left(x+5\right).$$

An integrating factor is

$$I(x)=e^{\int - 2 \cdot \left(x+5\right)\,\mathrm{d}x}=e^{- \left(x+5\right)^{2}}.$$

Multiplying through and using the product rule gives

$$\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}\left(e^{- \left(x+5\right)^{2}}\,z\right)=- \left(x+5\right) \cdot e^{- \left(x+5\right)^{2}}.$$

Integrating with respect to $x$, we obtain

$$e^{- \left(x+5\right)^{2}}z=\frac{e^{- \left(x+5\right)^{2}}}{2}+C.$$

Thus

$$z=C \cdot e^{\left(x+5\right)^{2}} + \frac{1}{2}.$$

Finally, substitute $z=y^{-1}$ and solve for $y$:

$$y=\frac{2}{2 \cdot C \cdot e^{\left(x+5\right)^{2}} + 1}.$$

Here $C$ is an arbitrary real constant; exclude singularities and restrict to the stated real intervals."] [:db/add "f42d077c-e368-53a5-991d-e999c0fb2c03" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] [:db/add "f42d077c-e368-53a5-991d-e999c0fb2c03" :question/answer-fields "37fce50a-669c-5904-b80e-2fbfd3c0cec3"] [:db/ensure "f42d077c-e368-53a5-991d-e999c0fb2c03" :question/validate] [:db/add 17592186147454 :knowledge-point/questions "f42d077c-e368-53a5-991d-e999c0fb2c03"] [:db/add "4d56d7e9-d563-5355-967b-957ca3f2b2b3" :answer/id #uuid "4d56d7e9-d563-5355-967b-957ca3f2b2b3"] [:db/add "4d56d7e9-d563-5355-967b-957ca3f2b2b3" :answer/type :answer.type/math] [:db/add "4d56d7e9-d563-5355-967b-957ca3f2b2b3" :answer/value "y=\sqrt[5]{C \cdot e^{\frac{10 \cdot \left(x+2\right)^{3}}{3}} - $$
\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}- \left(x+2\right)^{2} \cdot y=- \frac{3 \cdot \left(x+2\right)^{2}}{y^{4}}.
$$

Work on an interval where $\left(x+2\right)>0$. Choose constants and intervals on which the displayed expressions are real and finite.

{{selection}}"] [:db/add "c98ebde1-9cae-55b5-a3ae-6eb0a074c80f" :question/worked-solution "This is a Bernoulli equation with

$$\begin{aligned}p(x)&=- \left(x+2\right)^{2}\\ q(x)&=- 3 \cdot \left(x+2\right)^{2}\\ n&=-4.\end{aligned}$$

Divide by $y^{-4}$ and set $z=y^{5}$. The chain rule gives

$$\frac{\mathrm{d}z}{\mathrm{d}x}=5 \cdot y^{4}\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}.$$

Hence the linear equation in standard form is

$$\frac{\mathrm{d}z}{\mathrm{d}x}+\left(- 5 \cdot \left(x+2\right)^{2}\right)z=- 15 \cdot \left(x+2\right)^{2}.$$

An integrating factor is

$$I(x)=e^{\int - 5 \cdot \left(x+2\right)^{2}\,\mathrm{d}x}=e^{- \frac{5 \cdot \left(x+2\right)^{3}}{3}}.$$

Multiplying through and using the product rule gives

$$\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}\left(e^{- \frac{5 \cdot \left(x+2\right)^{3}}{3}}\,z\right)=- 15 \cdot \left(x+2\right)^{2} \cdot e^{- \frac{5 \cdot \left(x+2\right)^{3}}{3}}.$$

Integrating with respect to $x$, we obtain

$$e^{- \frac{5 \cdot \left(x+2\right)^{3}}{3}}z=3 \cdot e^{- \frac{5 \cdot \left(x+2\right)^{3}}{3}}+C.$$

Thus

$$z=C \cdot e^{\frac{5 \cdot \left(x+2\right)^{3}}{3}} + 3.$$

Finally, substitute $z=y^{5}$ and solve for $y$:

$$y=\sqrt[5]{C \cdot e^{\frac{5 \cdot \left(x+2\right)^{3}}{3}} + 3}.$$

Here $C$ is an arbitrary real constant; exclude singularities and restrict to the stated real intervals."] [:db/add "c98ebde1-9cae-55b5-a3ae-6eb0a074c80f" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] [:db/add "c98ebde1-9cae-55b5-a3ae-6eb0a074c80f" :question/answer-fields "46f8b52d-7488-5cfe-96a2-6f6270c23b92"] [:db/ensure "c98ebde1-9cae-55b5-a3ae-6eb0a074c80f" :question/validate] [:db/add 17592186147454 :knowledge-point/questions "c98ebde1-9cae-55b5-a3ae-6eb0a074c80f"] [:db/add "63a0a3f6-7a6e-53d0-870b-cb1f0d8e828e" :answer/id #uuid "63a0a3f6-7a6e-53d0-870b-cb1f0d8e828e"] [:db/add "63a0a3f6-7a6e-53d0-870b-cb1f0d8e828e" :answer/type :answer.type/math] [:db/add "63a0a3f6-7a6e-53d0-870b-cb1f0d8e828e" :answer/value "y=\left(C \cdot e^{\frac{3 \cdot x}{2}} + \frac{1}{3}\right)^{2}"] [:db/ensure "63a0a3f6-7a6e-53d0-870b-cb1f0d8e828e" :answer/validate] [:db/add "27053826-774a-5778-a46c-55339c8259ad" :answer/id #uuid "27053826-774a-5778-a46c-55339c8259ad"] [:db/add "27053826-774a-5778-a46c-55339c8259ad" :answer/type :answer.type/math] [:db/add "27053826-774a-5778-a46c-55339c8259ad" :answer/value "y=\left(C \cdot e^{\frac{x}{2}} + 3\right)^{2}"] [:db/ensure "27053826-774a-5778-a46c-55339c8259ad" :answer/validate] [:db/add "7920eb08-55a3-5637-8b43-d9eaab143d01" :answer/id #uuid "7920eb08-55a3-5637-8b43-d9eaab143d01"] [:db/add "7920eb08-55a3-5637-8b43-d9eaab143d01" :answer/type :answer.type/math] [:db/add "7920eb08-55a3-5637-8b43-d9eaab143d01" :answer/value "y=\left(C \cdot e^{\frac{x}{2}} - $$

$$ Take $y>0$. For even powers and powers of $2/3$ in the choices, retain only intervals where the base is positive. Choose constants and intervals on which the displayed expressions are real and finite.

{{selection}}"] [:db/add "63e30119-1a5b-5cbc-bb91-0a68fadb5bb2" :question/worked-solution "This is a Bernoulli equation with

$$\begin{aligned}p(x)&=-1\\ q(x)&=2\\ n&=\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}$$

Divide by $y^{\frac{1}{2}}$ and set $z=y^{\frac{1}{2}}$. The chain rule gives

$$\frac{\mathrm{d}z}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{1}{2 \cdot \sqrt{y}}\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}.$$

Hence the linear equation in standard form is

$$\frac{\mathrm{d}z}{\mathrm{d}x}+\left(- \frac{1}{2}\right)z=1.$$

An integrating factor is

$$I(x)=e^{\int - \frac{1}{2}\,\mathrm{d}x}=e^{- \frac{x}{2}}.$$

Multiplying through and using the product rule gives

$$\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}\left(e^{- \frac{x}{2}}\,z\right)=e^{- \frac{x}{2}}.$$

Integrating with respect to $x$, we obtain

$$e^{- \frac{x}{2}}z=- 2 \cdot e^{- \frac{x}{2}}+C.$$

Thus

$$z=C \cdot e^{\frac{x}{2}} - 2.$$

Finally, substitute $z=y^{\frac{1}{2}}$ and solve for $y$:

$$y=\left(C \cdot e^{\frac{x}{2}} - 2\right)^{2}.$$
